targetText: artillery had been furnished by the subscriptions of the National Guard. As their private property, it was officially recognized in the capitulation
summary: National Guard ownership of Paris artillery: exposing Thiers's attempt to steal worker-funded weaponry.
explanation: Marx details how Paris workers had paid for their own cannons by public subscription during the Prussian siege, proving Thiers's raid on Montmartre was illegal state plunder.

targetText: glorious working men's Revolution of March 18 took undisputed sway of Paris. The Central Committee was its provisional government
summary: The triumph of March 18: working-class insurrection establishing the Central Committee as provisional government.
explanation: When regular troops fraternized with Parisian workers at Montmartre, Thiers and his administration fled to Versailles, leaving the Central Committee of the National Guard in power.

targetText: General Lecomte, had four times ordered the 81st line regiment to fire at an unarmed gathering in the Place Pigalle, and on their refusal fiercely insulted them. Instead of shooting women and children, his own men shot him
summary: Soldier fraternization at Montmartre: troops executed counter-revolutionary commanders ordering massacres.
explanation: Regular soldiers refused General Lecomte's orders to open fire on Parisian women and children, joining forces with the workers and executing their commander.

targetText: magnanimity of the armed working men : so strangely at variance with the habits of the "Party of Order"
summary: Proletarian magnanimity vs bourgeois brutality: Paris workers treated reactionary opponents with leniency.
explanation: Marx contrasts the humane conduct of the revolutionary workers who allowed reactionary police and officials to retreat unmolested with the murderous violence of the bourgeoisie.

targetText: guilty of a decisive mistake in not at once marching upon Versailles, then completely helpless, and thus putting an end to the conspiracies of Thiers
summary: The strategic error of March 18: failing to march on defenseless Versailles immediately after victory.
explanation: Marx identifies the Central Committee's major strategic mistake: refusing to press the offensive against Versailles immediately allowed Thiers time to regroup counter-revolutionary forces.

targetText: captured soldiers of the line were massacred in cold blood; our brave friend, General Duval, the iron-founder, was shot without any form of trial
summary: Versaillist slaughter of Communard prisoners: Thiers's army executed captured worker-generals without trial.
explanation: Marx documents the immediate atrocities committed by Versailles troops under Thiers and Galliffet, who routinely executed captured Communard officers and soldiers.
